newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants better security before Schengen deal.
newsitem.headline: France wants better security before Schengen deal.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Saturday that progress must be made on European internal security before the Schengen accord on the free movement of people could be applied.

"Within the framework of the Schengen accord...migratory movements are a source of concern, which has led the government to refuse for the past two years the straight application of the Schengen accord which is, one must say, pretty angelic," De Charette told the newspaper Le Figaro in an interview.

"In the (EU) Intergovernmental Conference debate, this question is raised again. We demand a simple rule: that progress on free movement in Europe be preceded by progress on security, anti-terrorism, drugs and organised crime," he said.

The Netherlands, which holds the revolving EU presidency, proposed last month that the 1985 Schengen Agreement lifting passport controls among members be brought into the EU treaty when a new one was agreed later this year.
"Why not have free movement in Europe? But on the condition that real progress be made previously on matters of internal security," De Charette said.
The pact between mostly EU countries drops border controls and enhances cooperation on police matters.
